# Agent VM implementation

## Current Status

- Lifecycle: active.
- Implementation: protocol 4 explicit live-memory adjustment and the 48-GiB logical RAM ceiling are installed and observed with the archived source below. Protocol 3 reclamation/count-policy and retention results below are historical baseline evidence. PR readiness remains bound to current delivery validation and review evidence.
- CT base layer: Arch Linux, Incus resources and KVM present; this is not CLI/lifecycle acceptance.

## Live memory implementation and acceptance

The implementation provides explicit memory-only native live adjustment, pressure-independent reduction, guarded growth and conservative partial-failure accounting without automatic restart/stop. CPU/RAM ratios are 4/4 over unchanged 15-vCPU/12288-MiB bases, yielding 60 vCPU/49152 MiB; these are logical allocation ceilings. The daily Skill directs voluntary downsize after high-memory work when remaining workloads fit, preserving disks/cache and explicit lease renewal.

Initial native 4-to-2-GiB shrink and later 12-to-4-GiB shrink attempts returned convergence timeouts despite subsequent guest memory changes. Those errors remain failed evidence. The corrected shrinking path waits once for 45 seconds before its sole guarded completion; growth/hotplug is never retried automatically. Offline tests cover partial accounting/replay, pressure and unavailable metrics, boot/lease continuity, mode/protocol rejection and expiry/drain/configuration/reservation changes during settlement.

After production leases naturally ended at `2026-10-07T06:23:28Z`, the deployment owner installed the correction from `57b098ed252f7dcedfb6f8ce8237e6a89a6771ab`: control SHA256 `9d3665069a6d09d02084bfc4252f822f00fb3bd9345e4531b4661433693814f1`, CLI SHA256 `4ae8db7a9c7e4ca6fe9dfe27758fec0ceb428abc05a8f58907c65f76049eac1c`, protocol 4/version `0.4.0-native`. The earlier accepted RAM configuration change is ratio 2 to 4; the final control correction preserved that configuration, CPU/base budgets, native units, state and unrelated project settings. The parent independently checked installed source hashes. Health/default admission passed before drain exit; no runtime-home deployment or PVE access occurred.

In an independent project/config/database, an idle 8-vCPU/12-GiB VM completed 12-to-4-to-12-GiB live adjustment with this control. Shrink preserved the first native timeout (`currently 11003MiB`) and a successful second acknowledgement after settlement; growth succeeded once. Conservative reservation cleared only after completion. Boot identity `496f0259-ed6a-4b89-8dd0-a5dae3e8ff0a`, QEMU PID `462650`, background services, an existing 180-second SSH, lease, port and 20-GiB disk remained unchanged. QEMU RSS fell from 1099448 to 1080452 KiB on this already lightly resident guest; that observation does not claim 8 GiB of physical memory was resident or freed. Raw positive evidence is separate from the failed predecessor and the exact isolated resources were cleaned.

The same corrected control also started four low-residency VMs in a separate project/database with 4+10+10+10 GiB configured memory. Both native configuration and allocation records summed to 34816 MiB, above the CT-visible 32768 MiB and below the 49152-MiB ceiling; all four were Running and actual memory pressure was false. The parent independently inspected the archived source hash and raw doctor/native records. No large memory fill or production OOM was induced.

The parent used the candidate CLI for its unique production task: acquire/reuse, source synchronization, an Alpine Docker command, live 4-to-2-to-4-GiB changes across one SSH connection, byte-exact download/online tar export, final downsize, lazy release and cache reacquisition all passed. Generation changed only on reacquisition, cached data survived and resource/lease/NAT assertions held. These observations establish actual client/guest use; document checks do not prove every future Agent follows the instruction policy.

## Retention and voluntary-release instructions

The candidate [daily Skill](https://github.com/IvanLi-CN/agent-toolkit/blob/main/skills/agent-vm/SKILL.md#retain-and-renew) owns the retention, explicit-renewal and closure procedure. The [shared engineering workflow](../../../skills/project-engineering-workflow/SKILL.md#step-6-post-merge) calls it at post-merge and actual task closure, while readiness handoffs use the retention policy. [REQ-AGENT-VM-009 and VER-AGENT-VM-006](SPEC.md#req-agent-vm-009--skills-and-operations) own the contract and document validation. This is an instruction change, not a new CLI/control/timer implementation or deployment. Runtime home and production VMs are untouched; document checks do not establish live model compliance.

The candidate-document inspection scenarios are:

| Scenario | Required instruction outcome |
| - | - |
| Validation ends; further VM work or build-cache reuse is likely | Retain the session VM. |
| CI/review/owner-feedback wait, PR publication or readiness handoff with expected follow-up | Retain; report intended reuse and server deadline at handoff. |
| Agent actively tracks the task and needs more lease time for follow-up, with no guest command running | Explicit renewal is allowed within existing limits. |
| Drain refuses renewal, or the Agent returns control/is interrupted | No independent keepalive or continuing-renewal promise; expiry remains the fallback. |
| PR merged with no further VM work; remote-only CI/release tracking remains | Retrieve required data, release and verify closure; continue external tracking. |
| PR merged but VM verification remains | Finish the VM work before closure. |
| Non-PR task completes without expected follow-up, or task is cancelled/ends further VM use | Retrieve required data, release and verify closure. |
| Lease already ended or expired | Report observed cause and cleanup state; do not reacquire or renew for a closure claim. |
| Release dispatch succeeds but mappings/stop are unconfirmed or cleanup fails | Report incomplete/unverified closure rather than successful release; no implicit operations authority. |
| Release completes and the stopped cache remains | The cache is immediately reclaim-eligible; destroy still requires explicit discard authorization. |

## Reclamation and instance-admission acceptance

The accepted policy gives a stopped, fully cleaned, no-effective-lease cache no minimum retention period and removes the managed project's global instance-count ceiling. Manual GC selects all eligible caches regardless of age, remains dry-run by default and requires explicit application; the age timer independently retains its 24-hour selection threshold. Installed protocol 3 implements these corrections with shared object-locked eligibility, independent timer selection, count-policy preflight and default-request diagnostics. Candidate-matching installation and real acceptance pass. The detailed [reclamation design](RECLAMATION-DESIGN.md) records the settled requirements, deployment boundary and acceptance cases.

Read-only inspection on 2026-10-05 observed `agents` configured with `limits.instances=8`, two running guests and six stopped caches. Durable acquisition errors explicitly record the native maximum-instance refusal. Disk headroom was sufficient, so disk-triggered reclamation did not remove caches. At that diagnosis, installed protocol 2 lacked count-policy preflight and its manual GC shared the age timer's 24-hour filter; request-triggered disk reclamation already permitted younger eligible caches. Its generic `doctor.admission_ready` did not establish that allocation ceilings had room for a new request.

The observed running allocation was 12 vCPU and 24576 MiB, exhausting the accepted RAM ceiling independently of instance count. Count-limit removal must not be reported as solving RAM exhaustion. No native configuration or VM data was changed during this diagnosis.

## Implementation Coverage

Protocol 3 retains the protocol-2 separation of verified CT-local base budgets from multiplied allocation ceilings. Initial bases 15 vCPU/12288 MiB and ratios 4/2 yield 60 vCPU/24576 MiB. CT root cgroup metrics and verified LXCfs meminfo determine actual memory admission, without PVE or ancestor resource inspection. Stopped caches are excluded, transitions retain conservative reservations, and logical admission precedes disk reclaim or native interruption. Aggregate Incus project CPU/RAM quota conflicts are explicit errors; the deployment upgrade removes only those two keys under drain.

Acquire accepts CPU/RAM/disk fields, retains omitted cached sizes and reports active-lease differences without interruption. New and cached startup verify native disk and guest filesystem sizes. Read-only observations distinguish a valid lease from a running guest and leave unexpected-stop causes unknown without attributable evidence. Pressure or invalid observations do not block existing lease operations.

The offline suite covers ratio flooring, CT-only memory provenance and bounds, quota conflicts, cache accounting, atomic concurrent reservations, pre-effect rejection, pre-native rollback, expiry fencing, configurable acquire, cached age and protocol/journal compatibility. It comprises 85 client/control tests, including young-cache selection, generation races, partial deletion/reconciliation, count-policy conflicts and default-admission diagnostics, alongside the existing 12 synchronization and 4 migration tests. These fixtures are assessed separately from real deployment observations.

## Native lifecycle baseline observations

The following observations belong to the protocol-1 delivery in PR #159. They establish historical native lifecycle coverage and are not current protocol-3 deployment or empirical acceptance. In particular, the older CT memory observation and project aggregate quotas below are baseline facts rather than the new allocation policy.

The command contract is archived in `contracts/cli.md`. Daily and operations responsibilities live in the public `agent-toolkit` Skills [`agent-vm`](https://github.com/IvanLi-CN/agent-toolkit/tree/main/skills/agent-vm) and [`agent-vm-ops`](https://github.com/IvanLi-CN/agent-toolkit/tree/main/skills/agent-vm-ops). Fresh control/client drafts have been imported into this candidate; subsequent corrections belong only to candidate source. The deployment owner installs archived candidate copies; full VM acceptance requires the parent's direct observations with matching installed files.

The candidate implements one-shot SSH management, durable operation records, explicit generation-aware leases, native NAT, stopped-cache reclamation, conservative resource reservations and a guarded source-sync commit. Capacity admission measures only the CT-local Incus pool filesystem. External storage probes and their mandatory admission dependency have been removed; legacy probe configuration is rejected without execution. Offline fixtures verify those boundaries; they are not evidence of actual Incus behavior or deployment acceptance.

Preflight exposed that Incus 7.5.1 rejects global `--project` flags on raw `query` commands. Candidate source now supplies project identity only in the API URL and tests enforce that subprocess contract. The correction is installed from `6f0d6e9a34215f1ac688bf3c36ffcef5c567d30d`; independent CT verification matches control SHA256 `6579b9e7473adf20f19c79e0c74d7bd34dd58ba9bedc4bddfd2abeaa99e0b693`. The parent task actually ran the installed CLI: `doctor` no longer reports query errors, and `status` reports absent/no effective lease. Changes to protected connection-material wording do not introduce a registration system or role credentials.

The host alias independently resolves to root at `192.168.31.19:22` with strict checking. Installed client/control communicate over the existing SSH service. The deployment owner verified native units, the 15-minute calendar, the root-owned isolation ACL and absence of resident custom control processes. These preflight observations do not establish guest access, network isolation or expiry behavior.

The deployment owner verified 16 CPUs in CT affinity and a project CPU limit of 16; the configured admission budget is 15, reserving one CPU for the host. CT memory visibility is 16 GiB and the project limit is 32 GiB; the configured budget is 12288 MiB, reserving 25% of the smaller capacity. The parent independently verified these configuration fields and root-owned mode 0600. The default 2-CPU/4-GiB guest fits these budgets. The CT-local correction is installed from `5efeba1c50c90cae131831396cf69106aadf304f`, control SHA256 `1616d0ac2852796d428fbc5044bed6d7ac7e401f931deca432e8b04d05d4be46`; the parent actually observed `scope: ct-filesystem` from the installed CLI. The external capacity dependency is removed.

Image preparation exposed a separate preflight defect: an unavailable configured fingerprint did not prevent `doctor` from reporting ready. Candidate control now verifies exact image identity and VM type during preflight and before a fresh allocation can reclaim caches or create a VM. The guard is installed from `c62e4c0ec27e7cda647e581a30524e5b3d39c671`, control SHA256 `a6a144d119031d1db114e15e59fb4a9ee0029b7551def9432dc2f94f7fdfabee`, independently checked by the parent.

The deployment owner prepared Debian 13 fingerprint `4b2ddc09353aec82c77770c3868690649351e8438252bb01823eed548f423d86`, verified required tools, Docker/Compose, network-online and SSH/Docker/containerd services, and confirmed two fresh clones have different host keys. Temporary VMs and intermediate images were cleaned within their exact owned scope. The parent actually ran installed `doctor` with that pin: `ready: true`, no issues, CT-local capacity only. Candidate defaults and the installed configuration match the verified pin.

The parent's first real acquire from `88f3af2c760e91a588a3f40273c138c4d8b300b3` failed because the VM agent was not yet running. Cleanup stopped the guest and retained a port-free cache. Candidate acquisition, restart and restarting resize now use bounded native `incus wait` for agent and IPv4 readiness, capped by the current lease and followed by state/generation checks; they do not add a control-owned polling loop or extend the lease. The deployment owner installed this correction before the parent's next acquisition.

That acquisition exposed the restricted project's default proxy-device prohibition. Within the native NAT deployment scope, the deployment owner changed only `agents` project `restricted.devices.proxy` to `allow`, preserving its other restrictions and quotas. Candidate preflight now checks this exact permission before admission. The parent then acquired the cached VM successfully: active generation 3, guest IP `10.250.19.20`, SSH mapping `192.168.31.19:20000`, with a server deadline of `2026-10-04T16:01:24+00:00`. This proves acquisition and mapping creation, not the remaining guest-use and expiry assertions.

Installed root SSH and remote exit-status propagation are observed. The first synchronization run failed before remote mutation because the installed client's Python lacks `hashlib.file_digest`. Candidate hashing now uses standard streaming SHA256 on both sides, preserving manifest verification without a Python 3.11 dependency. The deployment owner installed helper SHA256 `ec4b0f8b2c212185fbb37755e5c55b542f07093954d74f77b886272f064b5d3e`; the parent synchronized 1495 files twice, confirming stale source removal, `.git` exclusion and adjacent result preservation.

The parent also observed root native SSH, a successful Alpine 3.22 Compose workload, byte-identical upload/download and online-only tar export. TCP `20001` and UDP `20002` mappings carried actual LAN traffic; a conflicting explicit allocation was rejected and both mappings became unreachable after exact removal. Repeated acquire and these operations preserved the lease deadline. One explicit renewal added 15 minutes.

Real disk growth exposed a native visibility requirement: root configuration changed from 20 to 21 GiB but the running guest still saw a 20-GiB block device. The attempt returned `resize_partial`, never success. Candidate resize now requires explicit restart allowance for any resource change, including disk growth, and returns an unapplied plan before reclaim or mutation when absent. After restart it verifies agent/network readiness and guest filesystem growth; an explicitly requested unchanged disk size also verifies or repairs growth. Partial error details remain available after stopped cleanup.

The installed control from `79313f17b8f35a98f263670d90b29da7255e8172` matches SHA256 `f9596203acff2fd3a692747324f87396f26bb5290210ad8be9f46ff16e922652`. The parent verified the unapplied disk plan, then explicitly allowed restart. Resize completed in 34.209 seconds: guest block capacity `22548578304` bytes (21 GiB), ext4 capacity `21675147264` bytes, and unchanged lease deadline. The filesystem grew during restart before the helper's idempotent verification. Reservations and the partial error cleared after verified completion.

Lazy release completed in 1.352 seconds; an existing SSH with one-second keepalive detection exited after 1.353 seconds. New connections were rejected and mappings were empty. Duplicate release preserved `inactive_since`. Reacquisition reused the same instance with generation 4, restored SSH alone and retained the test result; the parent released it again at server time `2026-10-04T16:09:47+00:00`. It is a stopped cache, not an active lease. These release observations do not replace short-lease expiry and ControlMaster acceptance.

The deployment owner exercised the unchanged installed control in an isolated project and pool, and the parent inspected the resulting raw records. Positive CT-to-guest TCP/UDP traffic, laptop-to-mapped-SSH traffic, guest DNS and an Alpine pull succeeded. Peer-to-peer access to the same positively tested listener, reflection through the CT's LAN address, and access to bridge management SSH failed as intended. The parent retained `network-positive-negative.json` in its external evidence set; the earlier incomplete harness is preserved separately and is not counted as a pass.

The production-equivalent isolated expiry timer used the persisted absolute lease deadline, `Persistent=yes`, one-second accuracy, zero randomized delay and a task/generation token. The parent inspected `expiry-evidence-oncalendar-2.json`: at the `2026-10-04T17:18:14Z` deadline, native proxy removal and exact conntrack clearance were observed within 1.010 seconds, and Incus STOPPED/cache state within 1.543 seconds. Matching established flows existed before expiry; no global conntrack flush was used. An independent laptop LAN observer received an SSH banner before expiry and could not complete connections afterward. New SSH and late renewal were rejected. Earlier relative-timer results are auxiliary evidence only.

Client detection is distinct from server withdrawal. A default ControlMaster and long SSH did not exit naturally within their 20-second observation windows, and the raw LAN holder did not receive EOF within its bound; those latencies remain lower bounds, not successful fast-disconnect measurements. The server entry-withdrawal and stop targets were measured directly. Client keepalive settings were not changed to improve the expiry result.

An old generation-1 timer left generation 2 active. In the separate same-generation experiment, explicit renewal moved the deadline from `17:32:45Z` to `17:32:55Z`; the timer arriving after the former deadline returned `rearmed/not-expired`, and actual Incus Running state and its exact NAT mapping remained intact. `renew-timer-same-generation-3.json` contains the worker results and native observations. Earlier invalid-generation, scheduling and test-unit cleanup attempts are retained without being treated as passing evidence. Exact proxy-removal fault injection also produced `cleanup_incomplete`, still stopped the guest and retained port/error records; applied reconciliation then reached a port-free cache without resetting its age.

The isolated control process was then actually SIGKILLed after its preparing record and reservation were durable, with the VM Running and its SSH proxy present. Applied `boot: true` reconciliation withdrew the proxy and port records, stopped the VM and cleared reservations while preserving all original ownership metadata. The parent inspected `process-interruption-boot-evidence-2.json`; exact destruction subsequently left an empty test inventory. No CT reboot was performed. Some supplemental harnesses recorded `finished_at` before dispatch, so those fields are not command-duration evidence; state assertions and independent native expiry observations are assessed separately.

A second real interruption, immediately after durable reservation and before timer creation, exposed a recovery defect: native disable rejected the nonexistent timer and left the task closing with reservations held. `recovery-missing-unit-evidence.json` preserves the failure before exact test-only cleanup. Timer removal now accepts this case only after native `not-found/inactive` state, empty fragment/unit-file properties and absence of the exact file are verified. Loaded/active units, existing files and unavailable inspection still preserve the original failure. The correction is installed from `47a33987bcc43b66aff251112e9fa193ff0d9724`, control SHA256 `7c581c9149d1ed038d1e3a399aeb34d7e6b63ca75608598512baf95d2a1c19cd`, independently checked by the parent. Real pre-timer SIGKILL followed by boot reconciliation now reaches absent with no ports, reservations, native instance or manually created timer.

The corrected control also passed an absolute-timer rerun after a `PrivateTmp=yes` visibility preflight for its isolated configuration/state. At the `18:27:00Z` deadline, mapping removal and connection refusal were observed at 1.263 seconds, then native Stopped/cache state at 1.823 seconds. The timer service succeeded, late renewal was rejected and exact destruction succeeded. `expiry-oncalendar-fixed-4.json` retains the raw observations; earlier invisible-helper/config attempts are invalid harness runs and are not counted. The control change is confined to the missing-unit error path; the inspected unchanged lifecycle, network and reclaim paths retain their earlier scenario evidence.

Real reclamation observations include stable release age, old-only 24-hour GC, oldest-first pressure reclaim and refusal after insufficient reclaim. Two stopped 20-GiB guests occupied `1651384320` and `1651380224` bytes in their exact CT-local VM directories. A new admission reclaimed only the older cache and preserved the newer directory; a deliberately unreachable test watermark then rejected creation after eligible reclaim. Effective leases, transitional records and an actual stopped unmanaged VM survived their protection scenarios. During real 21-GiB resize, the target's durable reservation remained protected and cleared only after native/guest capacity verification. All test watermarks, ages and costs belonged to isolated configuration/state; production clock, lease defaults and filesystem capacity were not altered.

Drain rejected new acquisition and renewal while preserving an existing lease and allowing release; exit restored admission. An unavailable CT-local capacity observation rejected acquisition with no new instance. The parent separately generated real ENOSPC by writing 2 MiB into a 1-MiB guest tmpfs: the installed CLI preserved exit code 1 and the diagnostic, removed that exact mount/directory and preserved the lease. The parent then synchronized the corrected source, verified its guest hash and released generation 5 in 1.368 seconds; the mapped port closed and duplicate release preserved age. This guest filesystem fault is not evidence that the CT filesystem was filled.

The deployment owner cleaned every exact isolated project/pool/network/profile/image/ACL, test unit and temporary directory. The parent inspected the copied raw records and final installed file modes/hashes. Native Incus and the age timer remain healthy; there is no deployed custom resident listener. Independent final inspection found three retained historical systemd slices active with `TasksCurrent=0`: these are empty metadata, not running test services. The parent cache remains stopped. SSH resolves to root at `192.168.31.19:22`; observed CT packages are Incus `7.5.1-1`, systemd `262-1`, OpenSSH `10.5p1-1` and conntrack-tools `1.4.9-1`, with no entries from `pacman -Qu`.

Offline validation passes: 44 client/control tests, 12 synchronization tests, 4 migration tests, fixed context checks (145 tests and Skill index), Skill format checks, migration scanning and Spec/document checks. Capacity tests verify CT-only measurement without command execution, rejection of removed probe configuration, invalid/unavailable local metrics and protected reclamation. Image-guard tests reject missing or non-VM images before allocation or cache reclamation. Native readiness tests check ordering, stopped cleanup after failure and expiry without implicit renewal; the project-permission test rejects a proxy prohibition before allocation. The synchronization suite verifies binary transfer and commit without the newer hashlib API. Resize tests model stale running-guest disk capacity and verify recovery after stopped cleanup and a new lease. Native timer-boundary tests cover the uncreated-unit recovery case and fail-closed behavior for conflicting or unverified state.

## Evidence Boundaries

- Host reboot behavior was exercised through the real boot-reconciliation action after controlled process interruptions; the CT was not rebooted.
- Client disconnect detection has only the separately recorded bounds above. There is no expiry recovery promise and no claim of ENOSPC prevention under overselling.
- Raw evidence is retained outside the source tree, including `/tmp/g6-20261005-evidence`, corrected recovery/expiry records and the parent's direct-use evidence set. Failed harnesses remain distinguishable from passing scenarios. Delivery readiness and formal review are tracked against the live PR, rather than inferred from these implementation observations.
- No PVE storage information is required or authorized; only the CT-local filesystem is part of admission and acceptance.
